brief.pitch: A scoping review of 51 independent text–biology foundation-model works shows the field has split into two cultures—tokenizing biology into language or encoding it into injected vectors—that keep systematically complementary information, are transparent in complementary ways, and whose self-reported "wins" (28 of 31 cross-culture comparisons) are almost entirely artifacts of proposing teams benchmarking their own method against unadapted opponents rather than evidence that either design is actually better.
brief.vision: A reader designing or reviewing the next text–biology foundation model can now name which culture they're building in, know exactly what information that choice discards and what it opaquely hides, demand the dependence tests and matched-opponent comparisons the field has mostly skipped, and apply the proposed neutral comparison protocol and reporting card to get a result that actually tells them which representation serves their task.
brief.most_arresting_asset: Fig5 (the cross-culture comparison panel: 28/31 wins for the proposing culture, collapsing to near-universal losses when opponents are self-built vs. near-universal wins when opponents are released/unadapted)

figures.claim: The two cultures are defined by what they keep: a cell as a rank-ordered list of ~100 gene names with zero opaque steps (token-native, 17 works) versus the same cell as 1-256 encoder vectors with a third of steps opaque (encoder-mediated, 16 works), shown against the field's year-by-year growth.
A PRISMA-ScR funnel taking 8,170 records down to 55 records / 51 independent works establishes the corpus is systematically assembled and recent, with no qualifying works before 2023.

Every input route in the corpus decomposes into combinations of just 22 reusable data operations, whose parameters are often unreported, and whose recurring motifs cleanly separate into verbalisation vs. encoder families matching the two cultures.

At the per-work level, token-native routes keep 50-1000 named genes but strip numeric values, while encoder routes compress hundreds-to-tens-of-thousands of features into 1-256 vectors inside learned modules -- a quantified, work-by-work picture of what each culture keeps versus hides, with unreported parameters equally common on both sides.

Both cultures name the same quantitative-information trade-off, but the field's comparative evidence is structurally biased: proposing cultures win 28 of 31 cross-culture comparisons (17 of 20 works) almost entirely against released, unadapted opponents, lose all 11 comparisons against self-built opponents, and the rare exceptions trace to scale or pretraining-data advantages rather than representation design -- meaning the evidence cannot yet settle which design serves a given task better.

A concrete, actionable fix is offered: a neutral comparison protocol (matched backbone, data, and budget; identity- and magnitude-level tasks; dependence controls) plus a reporting card for input representations, so future comparisons are no longer self-judged.

hook_verdict.fig1_is: A taxonomy/definitional panel: two cultures defined by what they keep (gene-name lists vs. encoder vectors) plus a year-by-year growth chart of the field.
hook_verdict.fig1_should_be: A compressed preview of the punchline trade-off itself: what each culture keeps/hides (from Fig4) sitting right next to the rigged-comparison result (Fig5's 28/31 collapsing to near-universal losses on self-built opponents). The growth chart is throat-clearing, not a hook.
hook_verdict.why: As described, Fig1 only tells the reader that two cultures exist and the field is growing -- a taxonomy claim, not a finding. The actual arresting result (self-judged comparisons are almost entirely artifacts) lives in Fig5, four figures later. A general-scientist reader skimming Fig1 would see a classification scheme and have no idea the paper's real contribution is an indictment of the field's evidence base. The paper is not fundamentally about 'there are two cultures' -- it's about 'nobody can currently tell you which one is better because the evidence is rigged,' and that has to be visible on page 1.

figure_moves.what: The core trade-off numbers (median 100 genes kept, no opaque steps vs. 1-256 vectors, 0.33 opaque steps)
figure_moves.why: This is the concrete, quantified version of 'what each culture keeps' that currently only shows up as a qualitative definition in Fig1. Putting the numbers in Fig1 turns a taxonomy panel into an evidence panel.

figure_moves.what: The headline 28/31 win-rate split by opponent type (self-built vs. released/unadapted)
figure_moves.why: This is the single most arresting number in the whole paper and the thing that actually motivates why the taxonomy matters -- it should be the second half of the hook, not held until figure 5.
Growth-over-time is corpus description, not a finding; it belongs with the PRISMA funnel as scoping-review mechanics, freeing Fig1 to carry the two load-bearing results.
Useful mechanism detail but should be visually subordinate -- a methods-adjacent figure rather than a main evidentiary beat; keep it but don't let it compete for attention with Fig4/Fig5.

missing_panels.what_to_show: A direct scatter/forest plot of each of the 31 comparisons plotting effect size (or win/loss) against a confound axis: opponent provenance (self-built vs. released-unadapted) crossed with scale/pretraining-data ratio, so the reader can see with their own eyes that wins track confounds, not representation.
missing_panels.analysis_needed: For each of the 31 comparisons, code opponent type, parameter-count ratio, and pretraining-data ratio; test whether win/loss is predicted by representation culture alone once these covariates are included (e.g., logistic regression or exact stratified test) -- this operationalizes the claim 'the rare exceptions trace to scale or data, not design' beyond the 3 anecdotal exceptions.

missing_panels.what_to_show: A task-stratified breakdown of the 31 comparisons (e.g., cell-type annotation vs. gene-function vs. generation/QA) showing whether one culture's advantage is task-dependent.
missing_panels.analysis_needed: Cross-tabulate comparison outcome by task category; report whether any task shows a non-confounded signal, since the paper's stated vision is helping a reader pick a representation 'for a given task.'

missing_panels.what_to_show: A worked example applying the proposed neutral comparison protocol and reporting card to one real pair of released models (post-hoc, matched backbone/budget), showing what the corrected comparison would have found versus what the original paper reported.
missing_panels.analysis_needed: Re-run or simulate a matched comparison on one accessible released token-native vs. encoder-mediated model pair under equalized backbone/data/budget; report the outcome delta versus the original self-reported result -- this converts Box1 from a proposal into a demonstrated fix.

missing_panels.what_to_show: The dependence-testing coverage (22/51 overall, 4/16 encoder-mediated) broken out per culture alongside the opacity numbers, since 'tested whether output depends on biological input at all' is as central to the transparency claim as opacity/quantitative loss.
missing_panels.analysis_needed: Stratify the 22/51 dependence-test figure by culture and by whether the work also made a cross-culture comparison claim, to show whether comparison-winners were even more likely to skip dependence testing.

kill_list.what: The raw 22-operation taxonomy detail (full list/names of all 22 operations) if shown as a standalone dense figure
kill_list.why: General-scientist audience does not need the full operational inventory in the main narrative; the headline claim ('everything decomposes into 22 reusable ops, split cleanly into two motif families') can be stated in one sentence with the figure demoted to supplement.

kill_list.what: PRISMA funnel exact record counts at every intermediate stage (8,170 -> ... -> 55/51)
kill_list.why: Needed for rigor/reproducibility but is standard scoping-review plumbing that doesn't advance the story; one summary number (8,170 down to 51 independent works) suffices in the main text/caption.

kill_list.what: The year-by-year growth curve as its own panel
kill_list.why: ‘The field is new and growing’ is a one-line fact, not a figure-worthy finding; fold it into the Fig2 corpus-description panel.

kill_list.what: Enumeration of the five groups (token-native, encoder-mediated, hybrid, language-conditioned, alignment-only) as a detailed standalone breakdown
kill_list.why: Only two cultures (token-native, encoder-mediated) carry the comparative-evidence story; hybrid/language-conditioned/alignment-only are long-tail categories (8+9+1 works) that dilute the two-culture framing if given equal visual weight.

arc.one_line: Two cultures keep systematically different biological information (named genes, zero opacity vs. compressed vectors, 1/3 opaque) -- and whoever 'wins' a head-to-head almost always just proposed the method.
Every input route in 51 works reduces to combinations of 22 reusable operations that cleanly sort into the two cultures, showing the split is structural, not incidental.
Quantified, work-by-work accounting of exactly what each culture keeps (gene identity vs. magnitude) and hides (opaque learned modules), with authors on both sides conceding the same trade-off.

The comparative literature is not neutral evidence: 28/31 cross-culture wins go to the proposing team, collapse to all-losses against self-built opponents, and the few real exceptions trace to scale/data, not representation.
A matched-backbone, matched-budget neutral comparison protocol plus a reporting card lets the next team (or reviewer) demand evidence that actually isolates representation design.
PRISMA-ScR funnel and corpus growth establish the review is systematic, recent, and complete enough to support the claims above.

review.boldest_defensible_fig1: A two-panel Fig1: (left) the quantified keep/hide trade-off per culture -- median 100 named genes, 0 opaque steps vs. median 32 vectors from up to 20,541 features, 0.33 opaque steps; (right) the win-rate indictment -- 28/31 proposer wins overall, collapsing to 0/11 against self-built opponents and near-universal wins only against released/unadapted opponents. This replaces 'here is a taxonomy' with 'here is what's at stake and here is why you can't trust the literature's answer yet' -- the actual spine of the paper, defensible because every number is already computed and reported later in the draft (Fig4 and Fig5); Fig1 is simply where they should first appear.
